task.title: Add a main-thread-authoritative Emacs agent interface mode
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1025 with a bounded, read-only, model-neutral Emacs and Org interface that does not block the editor or grant arbitrary Emacs Lisp authority.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a read-only interface mode backed by deterministic typed JSON responses.
Expose explicit buffer and native Org heading/source-block context without changing source-buffer state.
Advertise power-user facilities without implying unimplemented authority.
Bound every synchronous request path and reject worker-thread editor access.

attempts.summary: Implemented the first typed interface and drove each operation through focused RED tests.
attempts.diagnostic: The package, context operation, native Org snapshot, and interface mode initially did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added capability discovery, explicit context snapshots, native Org metadata, deterministic JSON encoding, and a read-only special-mode dashboard.

attempts.summary: Corrected three independent review blocks around Emacs main-thread boundedness and state preservation.
attempts.diagnostic: Review probes found load-path discovery; unbounded buffer, request-list, section-vector, metadata, response-encoding, and diagnostic-format traversal; and changed Org match data.
attempts.patch: Replaced load-path scans with constant-time callable checks; added source-buffer and metadata caps; bounded request objects, section vectors, names, response strings, collection width, nesting depth, node count, and total JSON output; detected cycles; preserved match data; rejected worker-thread dispatch; and strengthened malformed-input, state-preservation, and deterministic-JSON tests.

outcome.summary: Vela now has a batch-tested, read-only Emacs agent interface whose current synchronous operations have explicit finite bounds. Expensive work and all future mutation authority remain outside this first protocol slice.

lessons: Emacs should own live editor state while long-running model, network, indexing, build, and compute work runs in external cancellable workers.
Short main-thread callbacks require cycle-safe request and response validation, pre-copy collection limits, bounded metadata, output, and diagnostics, and explicit document-size limits.
Review replaced request-time load-path discovery with constant-time callable-symbol checks so capability listing performs no package or filesystem scan.
Review bounded cyclic and oversized request alists, section vectors before copying, operation and key diagnostics, source-buffer traversal, and worker-thread access with fail-closed protocol errors.
Review bounded buffer and Org metadata plus deterministic response encoding, preserved Org match data, and added cycle, depth, width, node, and output budgets to the public encoder.
A semantic protocol is safer and more model-neutral than synthesized key sequences or arbitrary eval.
Capability metadata must distinguish callable facilities from protocol-exposed and authorized operations.
